prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: தமிழ் / বাংলা · Mixed Indic (language ta).
Grid: 4 columns × 4 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 17px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "மொழி" · longest unbreakable word 52px · one-line width 52px
  col 2: header "ভাষা" · longest unbreakable word 44px · one-line width 44px
  col 3: header "பேசுவோர்" · longest unbreakable word 77px · one-line width 77px
  col 4: header "குறிப்பு" · longest unbreakable word 128px · one-line width 521px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 480px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 479px.
Fixed: content, font, 17px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 480px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Compare languages by their Tamil and Bengali names, speaker counts, and brief notes.","reading":"Read across each row to connect the two names with the speaker count and note; scan down the speaker column to compare counts.","groups":["Columns 1 and 2 give the same language name in two scripts and should have comparable visual weight.","Columns 3 and 4 pair a quantitative speaker count with qualitative context."],"keep_intact":["Language names and column headers","Speaker counts as complete values where possible","Individual words in the notes"],"may_wrap":["Notes in column 4 can wrap at word boundaries; their lines can use the height created by other wrapped cells in the same row."]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[73,65,98,243],"idea":"Give each short column its minimum one-line width and devote the remaining space to the notes."},{"name":"B","widths":[90,85,105,199],"idea":"Give the two language-name columns similar, generous widths while retaining enough space for naturally wrapped notes."},{"name":"C","widths":[76,68,145,190],"idea":"Emphasize the speaker-count column for comparison and use a narrower notes column that still fits its longest word."}]}
